Where twelve people actually sleep

Checked 10 Sep. The trip, girls and contrast columns are scored across all thirteen pairs. Lodging is not. Of the nine bases these pairs use, only two have a property researched at twelve people, and both were found by re-reading files already in the folder rather than by new research.

Everything in the corpus was sized for six people, two families of three. The trip is now twelve people in four families. That is why the lodging evidence looks absent when it is really scoped to the wrong group.

One price exists on this whole board: Plaka Collection on Naxos, €300 per villa per night for 1 June to 20 July. Everything else needs a direct quote.

Three things the pairs reveal

The resort end has already converged. Eight of the nine finish on Rhodes, Kos or Crete. Those are the only bases with the scale to absorb a longer stay, and the only ones where a fifteen-year-old can leave the property and reach something.

The town end is genuinely open. Ermoupoli, Naxos Chora, Pothia, Chania old town and Astypalea Chora are five very different answers to the same question, and the research does not settle between them. This is where taste decides, not more data.

Contrast and connection trade off directly. Every high-contrast pair is cross-cluster, and every cross-cluster link runs one to four times a week. The same geography that makes the Dodecanese feel unlike the Cyclades is what stops there being a daily boat.

The price of a trip that feels like two places is a thin, weekday-pinned crossing.

The Athens question

Three of the four recovered candidates, plus Naxos + Kos, are blocked by one thing only: no direct island-to-island link, so the route goes through Athens.

That blocker may not be real. Athens is already one of the three stops. If Athens sits in the middle of the trip rather than at the start, then "you have to connect through Athens" costs nothing extra — you were going there anyway.

Nobody has tested it. It needs the group to fly in and connect straight onward, spending Athens mid-trip instead of on arrival. If it holds, four pairs come back to life.

The short-stop idea, recorded

Josh, 10 Sep: "maybe we spend 2 days and 3 nights in a place if it's very slow?" — and separately, that 8–9 nights at the long stop is too much. Live and unsettled. Three consequences if it holds:

  • The release valve becomes a property of the long stop only. Three nights is not long enough for two fifteen-year-olds to grind each other down, so small quiet towns reopen as the short leg. This is what keeps Astypalea and Pothia on the list at all.
  • A short stop needs a better crossing than a long one, because half a day goes each way and losing a day out of three nights is proportionally brutal. Kalymnos + Kos at 35 minutes gains most; Syros + Crete gains least.
  • A short stop must be walkable from the bed. Pothia, Astypalea Chora and Ermoupoli pass. Leros fails — four separate settlements, commerce in one and charm in another, and no car-rental evidence for the island at all. That is why Leros is absent despite ranking 3rd and 6th on the trip criteria.

What would actually move this list

  1. Whether Athens can sit in the middle of the trip. The single biggest lever on the board. It decides whether R2, R3, R4 and pair 2 are alive or dead. One conversation with Ben and Phil, no research.
  2. A quote from Pefki Sea View Villas. The only property found anywhere that takes all twelve in one house and splits into two independent halves. Availability and price for the window are unknown.
  3. Anything on Kos at twelve people. Kos is the resort end of five of these pairs and the only named property sleeps six.
  4. A Naxos Chora property. Chora is the town stop in four pairs, including the two best-scoring ones, and nothing is named there at any size.
  5. What actually went wrong at Talloires — situational (bored, stuck, no escape) or ongoing between the two girls. Different answers imply different trips, and only the first is solvable by choosing an island. One question to Kristin.
  6. Cycladic lodging. Tinos, Sifnos, Amorgos and Andros have no group-lodging research at all. The Dodecanese is winning partly because it is the branch that got researched.

The constraints all of these sit inside

  • Twelve people, four families. Kids roughly 9, 10, 11 and 15 at travel time.
  • Three stops maximum — Ben and Phil do not want to move more than that.
  • Athens is one of the three and is already the biggest contrast in the itinerary, so the two islands must differ from each other or the trip is effectively one island with a ferry in the middle.
  • Every figure in the supporting research is a 2026 season used as a proxy. No 2027 rate or ferry timetable exists yet. Flights for summer 2027 are on sale now.
